blocks.text: AI Solution for Marketing

If you've tried using AI for business marketing, you've probably noticed something frustrating.

You ask for a promotional email or a social media post. The AI writes something. It looks okay at first glance, but when you actually read it, it's too generic, too formal, or just doesn't sound like your business.

Well, you're not alone — this happens too often when AI tools are used for marketing. But Jasper can solve this problem!
The Marketing Content Problem

Let's say you run a local bakery. You want to promote your weekend special — fresh croissants, 20% off Saturday morning. You open your go-to AI assistant and type: "Write a post about my weekend croissant special."
You get something like: "Indulge in our exquisite artisanal croissants this weekend. Crafted with premium ingredients and baked to perfection. Visit us for an unforgettable culinary experience."

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly. Usually, AI tools default to formal language because they're trained on a huge mix of content — including corporate marketing. If you don't guide them, they'll play it safe, and "safe" often sounds like big brands.

feedbackIncorrect.text: The grammar is fine, and length isn't the issue. The problem is tone — it sounds like a chain restaurant, not your neighborhood bakery. That's what happens when AI doesn't understand local business marketing.

blocks.text: To be fair, it wasn't wrong per se. It's just not you.

• Your actual customers don't talk about "exquisite artisanal" anything — they say "those buttery croissants" or "the chocolate ones."
  • And you'd never describe your bakery as a "culinary experience" — you call it "your go-to spot for fresh-baked treats."
So the tool didn't fail. It did what it could with a vague prompt and filled the gaps with generic marketing language.
Meet Jasper

This is where Jasper comes in. It's designed specifically for marketing content — not essays, technical docs, or open-ended conversation. Jasper's main advantage is that it helps you start with a marketing task (email, ad, social post) and guides you to provide the few details that actually change the result.
Think of it this way: General AI-assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) = Swiss army knife

• Useful for many tasks
  • You figure out how to use them for your specific task
  • Great for research, thinking, and analyzing
Jasper = Purpose-built marketing tool

• Designed specifically for business content
  • Organized around marketing tasks you actually need to do
  • Less flexible, but more efficient for its specific purpose
This becomes possible thanks to Jasper's specialized interface, where you can:

• Pick the type of marketing content you need (email, ad, social post)
  • Fill in a few details about your business
  • Get output that helps you start structured

Home Page
Home is your starting point. Here, you can start creating right away by specifying a writing task in the Jasper Chat.
Projects
The "Projects" tab helps you organize your work by client, campaign, or business area. This tab helps you to manage multiple marketing efforts.
Agent Library

The "Agent Library" tab is where you'll find Jasper's Agents — purpose-built AI tools for specific marketing tasks like emails, ads, social posts, and product content. So, instead of starting from a blank page, you can pick the type of content you need, and Jasper will guide you through what information to provide.
Jasper IQ
"Jasper IQ" tab is where you store context about your business, products, and brand, so Jasper can reference this information across all your content.

• ChatGPT: "I need to write an email promoting my weekend special at my bakery — 20% off croissants on Saturday morning. Can you help?"
→ ChatGPT asks questions, you clarify, it drafts, you request edits, and back and forth.

• Jasper: Open the Promotional Email Agent in the Agent Library → Add context, answer its questions — the email's primary goal, the main offers to highlight, and any custom instructions → Tap Generate now.
→ Jasper returns a structured draft on the first pass.

  • Ads: Facebook ads, Google ads, headline variations
  • Website content: product descriptions, service pages, "About" sections
  • Blog posts: articles that drive traffic and explain your expertise
  • Images: social graphics, ad visuals, and other marketing imagery
If it's something you'd post, send, or publish to promote your business — Jasper will handle it.

Content Creation Flow

In Lesson 1, you learned that Jasper is built for fast and structured marketing content. Now, let's make Jasper feel simple. 

When most people open Jasper, they see a lot at once: Agents, chat, documents, projects. It can be overwhelming to the point where you think: "Where do I even start?"

So, this lesson will show you the logic behind Jasper's workflow, so you can work efficiently instead of guessing.
Understanding Ways to Create Content
Jasper gives you two paths for creating marketing content:

• Chat — a flexible space for exploring, brainstorming, and refining
  • Agents ("Agent Library" tab) — structured formats for specific tasks
Most beginners default to chat because it feels familiar. But Agents can save you time when you already know what you're making (email, ad, product description, and so on).
Agents ("Agent Library" Tab)

Agents are pre-built formats for common marketing tasks. They reduce "blank page thinking" by asking for the inputs that matter. 

You can think of them as specialized tools in a toolbox — each one designed for a specific job.

So, when you open the "Agent Library" tab, you'll see a list of Agents with their names and short lines on what each does. To find the right one, type a task into the search bar or use the Filter button to narrow the list. There are more than 100 Agents. Let's look at how they work in practice.
Scenario: You're adding a new item to your online store — handmade candles — and you need a selling product description. So, you:

1. Open "Product Description" Agent and click use Agent
  2. Fill in the necessary information.
  3. Generate!
Jasper will produce a complete product description ready for your store.

Each candle is hand-poured with precision, reflecting a commitment to quality and sustainability. Agents Worth Starting With
You don't need to learn all of them. Start with a small set that matches what you create most often. Good starting points for small businesses and marketers: Email:

• Promotional Email (sales, offers, announcements)
  • Email Campaign (multi-email sequences)
Social media:

• Social Media Posts (organic posts for multiple platforms)
  • Instagram Caption (captions for your images)
Website & SEO:

• Product Description (benefit-led product copy)
  • Blog Outline (structured article planning)
  • Keywords (SEO keyword lists)
Polishing what you have:

• Content Improver (sharpen existing copy)
  • Content Rewriter (adapt one asset for another channel)
Rule of thumb: start with 2-3 Agents that match your most common tasks, then explore others as needs arise.

Understand Jasper IQ

No matter how long you work with an AI tool on your business needs, it'll often write content as if it's meeting your business for the first time. Jasper IQ fixes that by giving Jasper permanent knowledge about your business, so every piece of content reflects who you are. Let's dive into it!
The Generic Content Problem
Although Jasper is built for marketing copy, its outputs can sometimes feel generic, even when using Agents.

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly. Agents can structure the content, but they can't guess your product names, unique selling points, or brand voice. Without providing this information, Jasper will default to language that could fit almost any business.

feedbackIncorrect.text: The issue usually isn't quality or subscription level. When Jasper doesn't have a business context, it defaults to general marketing language that fits any company.

For a limited time, order our new seasonal drink and get a second one completely free. It's a great chance to treat a friend to a coffee date, or just enjoy a little extra for yourself. We can't wait to see you at the shop! [Come In and Taste It]

blocks.text: Meet Jasper IQ
This is where Jasper IQ comes in and saves the day! It lets you store business context in one place, so Jasper can use it while generating content.

Instead of explaining your context again in every Agent, you set it up once in Jasper IQ.

After that, any Agent can use it. You can choose your Brand Voice and Audience from a dropdown, or set them as defaults, so Jasper creates content based on that information.
In this sense, Jasper IQ is your business knowledge base, split into a few sections:

• Brand Voice: your tone and personality, so outputs sound like you and not a generic brand
  • Audiences: your customer segments, so content speaks to who you're actually addressing
  • Knowledge Base: your company info — products, pricing, locations, hours — uploaded so Jasper stays accurate
  • Style Guides: your rules for terminology, grammar, and punctuation
  • Visual Guidelines: your rules for imagery, so any visuals stay on-brand
Set these up once, and the information becomes available across all your projects and Agents.
Setting It Up Once
Setting up Jasper IQ is a one-time job. Open Jasper IQ from the sidebar, pick a section, and add your details.

Start with Brand Voice: click Add Brand Voice, give it a name, then add a few examples of content that already sounds like you — emails, posts, or other brand materials. You can paste the copy directly, share a link, or upload a document. Jasper reviews the samples and builds a voice from them.

Audiences work the same way. Click Add Audience, name a segment like "Portland locals," and add a short description or let Jasper generate one for you. Jasper expands it into a full profile of the group. You can also provide audience documentation, such as demographics or statistics, and customer stories.
Once your Brand Voice and Audiences are saved, you select them from a dropdown inside any Agent.
Or you can set them as defaults in Workspace settings, so they apply to everything automatically.

Nice. Now that your context is set, you can pull it into any Agent with a click.

From Blank Page to Published Post

In the previous lesson, you started a consulting service. Now, you've built a website for it, and you need a blog post that would show expertise, attract the right leads, and rank well in search. The topic is clear: "How to Know When Your Sales Process Needs Restructuring." But sitting at your keyboard, you face the classic issue: how do you organize all your insights without spending hours staring at a blank page?
The Long-Form Content Challenge

Long-form content (like blog posts and website content) works differently from emails or social posts.

With short content, you can often write your way into clarity. With long formats, that approach usually gets messy fast. Most people start writing and hope the structure emerges naturally — and it rarely does.

feedbackCorrect.text: The challenge is structure, organization, and focus. Good long-form content needs a clear framework before you start writing.

feedbackIncorrect.text: The real challenge is organizing your knowledge into a structure that guides readers logically through your insights without losing them.

blocks.text: This is where Jasper's approach to long-form content becomes powerful: structure first, then write. Start with Chat. It will help you map out your post's structure before writing a single paragraph.

blocks.exampleResponse: Introduction: Why sales leaders ignore warning signs until deals stall Five signals your process needs attention: — Pipeline bloat — Lengthening cycles — Rep confusion — Inconsistent wins — Customer complaints Next steps for restructuring (quick wins vs. full overhaul, getting executive buy-in) Conclusion: Small changes now prevent major problems later

blocks.text:
See what happened? Instead of brainstorming for hours, you now have a clear roadmap: five main sections with an introduction and a conclusion, a logical flow, and specific points to cover.

This outline can become your writing blueprint.
Now that you have a structure, it's time to turn this outline into actual content. For this purpose, you can use the "Blog Post" Agent and paste your outline as context.
The Agent expands your outline into full sections, grounded in your Jasper IQ context, and opens the draft in Canvas — Jasper's writing workspace.
Here, you can edit and add details, but you're shaping a complete draft instead of inventing the sequence from scratch.

blocks.exampleResponse: 5 Signals Your Sales Process Needs Attention — Your pipeline is bloated A big pipeline feels reassuring. But when it's stuffed with deals that haven't moved in months, it's not a sign of health—it's clutter. Bloated pipelines hide the truth about your real opportunities and make forecasting nearly impossible. If your reps can't tell you the clear next step for every deal in their pipeline, that's a red flag. — Your sales cycles keep getting longer Track how long it takes to close a deal today versus a year ago. If that number is creeping up, something in your process is creating friction. Maybe approvals take too long, maybe reps are chasing unqualified leads, or maybe your stages no longer match how customers actually buy. — Your reps are confused When salespeople aren't sure what to do at each stage, they improvise. That leads to inconsistent messaging, skipped steps, and deals that fall through the cracks. If you ask three reps how they handle a discovery call and get three different answers, your process isn't documented clearly enough. — Your wins feel inconsistent Some months you crush quota. Others you can't figure out what went wrong. When success feels random rather than repeatable, it usually means your process isn't driving results—your individual top performers are. That works until those performers leave. — Customers are complaining Pay attention when prospects say things like "I had to repeat myself three times" or "nobody followed up." These complaints point to gaps in handoffs, communication, or follow-through. A messy internal process almost always becomes a frustrating external experience.

Type what you want — "expand this with concrete causes" — and Jasper rewrites that part in place, leaving the rest of your post untouched.

blocks.exampleResponse:
Longer sales cycles rarely announce themselves — they creep in. A deal that closed in 60 days last year now takes 100, then 120, and everyone shrugs it off as "a slow quarter."

But the causes are concrete. Approvals sit in inboxes for days. Reps chase leads that were never qualified. Or your stages no longer match how buyers actually decide, so deals stall between steps with no clear owner.


The fix starts with measurement: track your average cycle length now, then break it down by stage. The stage where deals sit longest is where your process is leaking time — and that's where a tighter framework pays off first.

Here's the full workflow for blog and website content:

The topic is clear: "How to Know When Your Sales Process Needs Restructuring." But sitting at your keyboard, you face the classic issue: how do you organize all your insights without spending hours staring at a blank page?
The Long-Form Content Challenge

Long-form content (like blog posts and website content) works differently from emails or social posts.

With short content, you can often write your way into clarity. With long formats, that approach usually gets messy fast. Most people start writing and hope the structure emerges naturally — and it rarely does.

If that number is creeping up, something in your process is creating friction. Maybe approvals take too long, maybe reps are chasing unqualified leads, or maybe your stages no longer match how customers actually buy. — Your reps are confused When salespeople aren't sure what to do at each stage, they improvise. Articulating Value Clearly

A launch can fail for a surprisingly simple reason: people don't understand what you’re offering fast enough. Here, you'll learn how to use Jasper Chat to articulate value in ways that make people instantly understand your offer: what it is, who it's for, and why it matters.
Why Value Is Hard to Articulate

Most people struggle to explain their products clearly. They either list features like "4-week course with video lessons" or resort to buzzwords like "game-changing transformation". Neither approach works.

feedbackCorrect.text: All correct. The challenge is translating what you built into what customers actually get: clear outcomes, not feature lists or empty hype.

feedbackIncorrect.text: All correct. The goal is clarity: value in terms that customers immediately understand and care about.

blocks.instruction: Select all possible answers

options.label: Explaining what you built instead of what the customer gets
Using vague language that sounds impressive but says nothing
Confusing features with benefits

blocks.question: What makes a value statement particularly challenging?

blocks.text: So, a clear value statement should answer these three questions for the customer:

• What is it?
  • Who needs it?
  • What problem does it solve?
Features vs Benefits
Features describe what your product is. Benefits explain what your customer gets. Example:

• Feature: "4-week online course"
  • Benefit: "Learn practical frameworks you'll use immediately"

Let's practice with a concrete scenario. 

You're launching a project management course for non-PMs — people who run projects but lack formal training.

We'll use Jasper to translate a feature into a customer-focused benefit.

blocks.exampleResponse: Feature: Self-paced video lessons with downloadable templates Benefit: Learn on your schedule and apply frameworks to your actual projects as you go — no waiting for the next cohort or falling behind.
blocks.prompt: Complete to see how Jasper will convert a feature statement into customer-focused benefits.
blocks.template: Convert this feature into a customer benefit: "[feature statement]"

feedbackCorrect.text: Right! Customers don't buy "video lessons", they buy outcomes. Benefits translate your product into results they actually care about achieving.

feedbackIncorrect.text: It's not about emotion or premium positioning. Benefits work because they answer the customer's real question: "What do I get from this?"

options.label: Features are too technical for most audiences

Benefits explain the outcome customers care about
Benefits make products sound more premium

blocks.text: Good Work!
The benefit that Jasper wrote focuses on what the customer experiences (flexibility, immediate use) rather than what the product contains (videos, templates).
Starting with the Problem
Clear value usually starts with the customer's problem — the situation they recognize instantly.

• Not: "Comprehensive project management training"
  • Instead: "You run projects but have no formal PM training — here's what you need and it shows up in your timelines"
Let's practice identifying the real problem your product solves.

Now, let's pair that problem with your solution to create a complete value statement.

This course teaches practical frameworks for timeline management, stakeholder communication, and risk mitigation — designed specifically for non-PMs who lead cross-functional work.

blocks.text: The Hype Problem
When people struggle to articulate value clearly, they often compensate with "impressive" words: revolutionary, game-changing, cutting-edge. Without specifics, those words sound empty.
So, let's practice replacing hype with concrete value.

Building Your Brand with Consistency

Brand isn't built on one viral post or perfect bio. It requires the slower way: consistent voice, repeated positioning, and clear values communicated across everything you publish.

So, in this lesson, you’ll learn how Jasper's brand tools help you keep your voice and positioning steady.
What Is Brand Building?
Brand building is how you communicate your voice, positioning, and values across all platforms and content types consistently.

feedbackCorrect.text: Consistency is hard because you're creating content across platforms, trying to stay fresh, and often forgetting your own positioning. Jasper's brand tools help you stay aligned.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Uniqueness isn't as important as consistency. The challenge is maintaining your voice and positioning reliably across different formats and situations.

blocks.instruction: Select all possible answers

Keeping your positioning and values in mind every time you write
Needing to sound unique compared to everyone else

blocks.question: What do you think makes maintaining a consistent brand voice particularly challenging?

blocks.text: Strong brands feel recognizable everywhere. Weak brands feel scattered — formal on one platform, overly casual on another, and inconsistent in what they stand for.
Jasper can handle this through three tools:

• Brand Voice
  • Knowledge Base
  • Chat
Let's go through each one.

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! Brand Voice is about how you sound (direct, friendly, professional). Knowledge Base is about what you're known for (expertise, positioning, values).

feedbackIncorrect.text: These tools serve different purposes. Brand Voice is about how you sound (direct, friendly, professional). Knowledge Base is about what you're known for (expertise, positioning, values).

options.label: They do the same thing but in different sections
Brand Voice is optional; Knowledge Base is required
Brand Voice is for social media; Knowledge Base is for websites
Brand Voice controls tone; Knowledge Base stores your expertise and positioning

blocks.question: Before we elaborate, what do you think is the difference between Brand Voice and Knowledge Base?

blocks.text: Brand Voice
You've already seen Brand Voice earlier; it defines how your business or personal brand communicates: not what you say, but how you say it. Example:

• Formal: "I assist clients with strategic marketing initiatives"
  • Conversational: "I help businesses figure out what marketing actually works"
Same service, different voice.

Imagine you're a freelance product designer building your personal brand. You want your content to sound direct, practical, and problem-focused.

Let's set that up.

blocks.template: My brand communication style is [tone] and [approach]. I focus on [what you emphasize] and avoid [what you don't do].

blocks.text: Excellent!
Now every piece of content Jasper creates will maintain this voice — whether it's a LinkedIn post, portfolio description, or newsletter.

feedbackCorrect.text: Right! This contradicts the brand voice completely. It's vague ("beautiful"), focuses on aesthetics over function, and uses generic excitement rather than specific problem-solving.

feedbackIncorrect.text: The defined brand voice emphasizes practical problem-solving and real impact, not design trends or aesthetic excitement. This post sounds generic.

Doesn't match brand voice

blocks.text: Knowledge Base
Brand Voice controls how you communicate. Knowledge Base handles what you communicate — your positioning, expertise, and values. It can also be set up in the "Jasper IQ" section.

You can add knowledge in three ways: by pasting text, uploading files, or adding links.

Once it's in place, Jasper consistently stores facts about your expertise and can pull from it when generating content.

blocks.prompt: Add information about your positioning and expertise to the Knowledge Base.
blocks.template:
Core Expertise: [What you specialize in]
Professional Positioning: [How you're different]
Values: [What matters to you]
Recent Work: [Current focus]

blocks.text: Great! Now, Jasper has your brand foundation stored. Every piece of content will consistently reference this expertise and positioning.
Creating Brand-Aligned Content

With Brand Voice and Knowledge Base being set, you can create content that's consistent both in tone and positioning.

Let's see how they work together on the example of a LinkedIn post about a recent project.

blocks.exampleResponse:
Spent the last month redesigning a financial analytics dashboard that analysts actually hated using. The problem wasn't visual design — it was 47 different data filters with zero guidance on which ones mattered.

We reduced filters to 12 essential ones, grouped by use case, with smart defaults based on user role. Analysts went from 8 clicks to find what they needed down to 2.

This is what B2B product design actually is: solving messy problems that don't photograph well but make people's jobs easier.
blocks.prompt: Use Jasper Chat to create a LinkedIn post that reflects your brand.
blocks.template: Write a LinkedIn post about [project topic] that demonstrates [expertise area] in my brand voice

blocks.text:
See? This post reflects your Brand Voice (direct, practical) and references your Knowledge Base (B2B SaaS expertise, complex interfaces, usability focus).

This is the value of combining both tools: your content sounds like you, and it reinforces what you want to be known for.

  1. Brand Voice: Define tone and communication style.
  2. Knowledge Base: Store expertise, positioning, and values.
  3. Create consistently: Use Chat to generate brand-aligned content.
  4. Repeat core messages: Brand builds through consistent positioning.
Jasper scales your voice. The judgment and personality are yours.

blocks.text: Brand Voice
You've already seen Brand Voice earlier; it defines how your business or personal brand communicates: not what you say, but how you say it. Example:

  • Conversational: "I help businesses figure out what marketing actually works"
Same service, different voice.
